messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER DUTY - Incident 1783010001: Elevated DNS failures (authoritative delegations) affecting eu & apac customers. Severity: P1. Pager duty: @jon oncall.

jon: getting hit by a wave of NXDOMAINs from customers in APAC and EU about 07:22 UTC. Alerts: dns-resolution-errors-edges. Quick check: our authoritative servers are healthy locally but many public resolvers return old NS or timeouts.

rachel: saw error spike in nginx logs showing upstream DNS lookup timeout -> 504s, tenants using redwood.example and api.redwood.example. Support count rising.

devops-bot: automated check: tcp/tls to auth DNS servers ok, UDP responses inconsistent. EDNS results vary across vantage points.

jon: can someone run repeat dig +short from apac vantage?

leo: running from sydney probe:```
$ dig @ns1.redwood-dns.net redwood.example SOA +short
; connection timed out
$ dig @ns1.dnsmadeeasy.net redwood.example SOA +short
ns1.dnsmadeeasy.net. hostmaster.dnsmadeeasy.net. 2026031501 3600 600 604800 3600
```

leo: backup provider (dnsmadeeasy) is responding fine. Our primary auth seems to be petering out for some resolver clusters.

tasha: check provider status pages: Cloudflare shows "localized DNS resolution degradation" in EU and APAC. Route53: noting increased propagation times after a recent delegation update (we did a scheduled swap last night).

rachel: aha, last night a deployment rolled out an NS glue update for redwood.example to move to new Anycast nodes. Could this be a partial rollback or mis-ordered change leaving some registrars referencing mixed glue?

jon: good catch. I see the change in our infra audit: `ns-update batch 2026-03-14 23:58` applied, then another automated rollback attempted at 01:05 due to a separate test failure. It's possible registrar-level glue propagation ended up inconsistent.

devops-bot: runbook step: enable DNS failover to backup provider and reduce TTLs to 30s for both A/CNAME and NS records.

jon: I'll do a temporary delegation to DNSMadeEasy (we already have accounts). Plan: UPSERT NS on registrar via Route53 and update glue where possible, set NS TTL to 30, and simultaneously set edge router to use IP-based origin routing for eu/apac to avoid domain lookup for internal routing.

leo: making the Route53 change now (dry-run looks fine):```json
{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"redwood.example.","Type":"NS","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"ns1.dnsmadeeasy.net."},{"Value":"ns2.dnsmadeeasy.net."}]}}]}
```

tasha: I'll prep customer advisory draft: explain that DNS lookups in EU/APAC may fail due to propagation mismatch; recommend using 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 or our backup resolver 149.112.x.y for a bit.

rachel: also adding note: for customers with custom CNAMEs, advise temporarily lowering TTL and updating their registrars to include backup NS where possible.

jon: changing edge routing now to prefer direct IP origin for eu/apac pools. Command: `routerctl set-origin-policy --pool eu,apac --mode ip-prefer --duration 45m` — applied.

leo: Route53 UPSERT applied. Asking DNSMadeEasy to confirm zone sync. They responded: "zone imported and authoritative; we see queries from APAC/EU increasing."

devops-bot: synthetic probes now hitting both primary and backup NS every 20s. Alert threshold set: >8% failures in 10m triggers page.

jon: rolling forward a second mitigation: enable short-circuit TTL for internal clients to use our internal resolver overlay that returns backup A records when public lookup fails. Pushing config to internal-resolvers.

rachel: monitoring shows error rate dropping in Sydney probes but EU still noisy. Support inbound count stabilized after advisory published.

tasha: published advisory: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1783010001 - note posted at 07:40 UTC. Included workaround steps and ETA estimates.

leo: contacting registrars for glue refresh where possible. Some registrars allow immediate glue update; others respect registry caching windows. We're documenting which TLDs had slow registry-level propagation.

jon: handoff for next oncall (@rachel): current state: mitigation applied (backup NS active, edge ip-prefer, internal resolver overlay), customer advisory live, probes improving but not fully green in EU. Remaining tasks: keep monitoring, coordinate with vendors for root-cause (possible mixed glue from rollback), collect traceroutes for failed resolvers, prepare postmortem timeline.

rachel: acknowledged. I'll stay with thread and keep updates. If error rate >5% re-escalate to infra lead @leo.

devops-bot: checkpoint at 07:58 UTC: probe success APAC 96%, EU 91%. Support tickets: 12 open, 4 high priority.

jon: note for PM/postmortem: double-check canary rollback ordering and add preflight to detect registrar/registry-level inconsistencies before automated rollback. Also add an automated test that queries multiple public resolvers after delegations change.

leo: opening vendor tickets with Cloudflare/AWS to get packet captures and EDNS behavior logs. Also asking DNSMadeEasy to keep zone active as standby for 24h.

rachel: leaving final comment before handoff: status page will be updated every 30m until we see 99.9% probe success across regions for 1h. Postmortem owners: jon -> infra sequence/rollout, leo -> vendor liaison & glue, tasha -> customer comms, rachel -> operational runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
